title: A RANDOMIZED, PLACEBO-CONTROLLED, MULTICENTER, CLINICAL TRIAL OF COLCHICINE IN AMYOTROPHIC LATERAL SCLEROSIS (CO-ALS II)
official: A RANDOMIZED, PLACEBO-CONTROLLED, MULTICENTER, CLINICAL TRIAL OF COLCHICINE IN AMYOTROPHIC LATERAL SCLEROSIS (CO-ALS II)
summary: Main objective: to determine whether colchicine, administered at a dosage of 0.005 mg/kg/day, can slow disease progression compared to placebo
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Patients diagnosed with probable laboratory-supported, clinically probable, or definite ALS according to the Revised El Escorial criteria (Brooks, 2000) (both sporadic and familial forms)
2. Female or male patients aged between 18 and 80 years old
3. Disease duration from limb weakness or bulbar symptoms onset < or = 18 months at screening
4. Stable dose of Riluzole at 50 mg bid for at least 30 days prior to screening
5. BMI>17.5 Kg/m2
6. FVC≥60% of the predicted normal value for gender, height, and age at screening
7. Patients able to provide informed consent and willing to comply with study procedures
8. Use of highly effective contraception both for males and females
Exclusion criteria:
1. Prior use or prior allergy/sensitivity to colchicine
2. Women who are pregnant or breastfeeding
3. Participation in other RCTs within the last 30 days before screening
4. Chronic use of colchicine or other anti-inflammatory drugs (e.g. corticosteroids, methotrexate, IL1-1b antagonist, TNF-alpha inhibitor)
5. Food or co-medications (e.g. strong CYP3A4 inhibitors) that will result in elevated plasma level of colchicine
6. Inflammatory/autoimmune disorders or chronic infections or malignancy
7. Severe renal or liver failure, blood dyscrasia or white blood cells<4,000/mm³, platelets count<100,000/mm³, hematocrit<30%
8. Severe comorbidities (heart, renal, liver failure), autoimmune diseases or any type of interstitial lung disease, with severity determined at the investigator’s clinical judgment
9. Patients with ALSFRS-R total score<28
10. Patients with invasive ventilation or non-invasive ventilation > 8 hours/day
11. Patients with rare hereditary problems of galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption
